headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Windsurf can write/execute in shared local files while Airflow can egress broadly, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads/writes workspace files, uses clipboard and MCP, and can auto-execute commands; Airflow can consume APIs and broad egress but has no browser. A shared local filesystem or copied content creates a plausible injection bridge, though not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through the same workspace or clipboard, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled, malicious file content can influence command execution.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces or directories.
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf.
Require manual review of any file content before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files and send data to a model proxy or MCP servers; Airflow has broad network egress. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Windsurf can transmit them outward, while Airflow can also move data off-host.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, Windsurf can read them.
IF either agent is pointed at secrets or regulated data, broad egress can exfiltrate it.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace.
Restrict Windsurf to a non-sensitive project directory.
Block outbound network access except approved endpoints.
Rotate any credentials stored in workspace files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and Windsurf can execute shell, modify git state, and write the filesystem. In a shared local filesystem concurrency model, both can mutate the same repo or files without locking, making destructive write conflicts likely by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Airflow is also updating files, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf is a closed-source agentic IDE with tool use and command execution; Airflow can generate or move data via APIs. If Airflow outputs are treated as authoritative inputs for Windsurf, errors can cascade into edits, shell commands, or commits without robust verification.
conditions: IF Airflow-produced artifacts are fed into Windsurf without verification, incorrect facts can be operationalized.
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled, a bad upstream output can trigger immediate actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Windsurf acts on Airflow output.
Require schema validation for exchanged artifacts.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Limit Airflow outputs to non-actionable summaries.
requires-engineering: add signed, typed handoff contracts.

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available and shows no touched data classes, while Windsurf is closed-source and handles source code/open files with model-provider keys. The profiles do not show a specific residency or regulatory mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf's workspace, compliance obligations may expand.
IF Airflow is used to move regulated data into the same environment, retention and logging policies must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Avoid storing secrets in shared files.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
